_about: Hand-checked trip-planning facts for waterfall pages, keyed by page URL. Every field is optional: leave it out rather than guess. 'free' is true only when no entry or parking fee applies, false when one does. Prices and rules change, so each entry records the date it was checked and its sources.

/oregon/cascade-locks/multnomah-falls.hike: Lower viewpoint is a short paved walk from the I-84 Exit 31 lot; the trail to the top viewpoint is 2.4 miles round trip
/oregon/cascade-locks/multnomah-falls.elevationGain: About 600 feet to the top of the falls
/oregon/cascade-locks/multnomah-falls.difficulty: Easy to the lower viewpoint and Benson Bridge; strenuous, steep and uneven to the top
/oregon/cascade-locks/multnomah-falls.parking: I-84 Exit 31 lot (about 186 spaces) plus a small privately operated paid lot on the Historic Columbia River Highway; no shoulder parking on the highway
/oregon/cascade-locks/multnomah-falls.fees: No entry fee. A timed-use permit was required for the I-84 lot from 9 a.m. to 6 p.m., May 22 to Sept. 7, 2026 ($2 online transaction fee; limited free permits in Troutdale and Cascade Locks)
/oregon/cascade-locks/multnomah-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash, including the trail to the top; not inside the lodge
/oregon/cascade-locks/multnomah-falls.swimming: No; do not enter Multnomah Creek, which has spawning fish
/oregon/cascade-locks/multnomah-falls.accessibility: Paved path with slight inclines from the I-84 lot to the visitor center and lower viewing area; accessible parking at both lots
/oregon/cascade-locks/multnomah-falls.bestSeason: Winter and spring, when flow from Larch Mountain springs is highest
sources: Recreation.gov: Multnomah Falls timed use permit

/tennessee/chattanooga/ruby-falls.hike: Guided cave walk of about 1 mile round trip after a 260-foot elevator descent; allow up to 90 minutes
/tennessee/chattanooga/ruby-falls.difficulty: Easy to moderate: paved, mostly level, with about 50 steps in small groups
/tennessee/chattanooga/ruby-falls.fees: Timed tickets sold online only: $29.95 adults, $19.95 ages 4 to 12, $28.95 seniors 65+, free age 3 and under
/tennessee/chattanooga/ruby-falls.dogs: No pets in the cave (trained service animals only); free outdoor kennels seasonally, first come, first served
/tennessee/chattanooga/ruby-falls.accessibility: The cave is not wheelchair or stroller accessible; the Blue Heron Overlook, plaza, gift shop, cafe and restrooms are
/tennessee/chattanooga/ruby-falls.bestSeason: Year-round; the cave is underground, so weather matters little

/washington/snoqualmie/snoqualmie-falls.hike: Upper viewing platform is about 200 feet from the paid lot; the trail to the lower viewpoint is 1.4 miles round trip
/washington/snoqualmie/snoqualmie-falls.elevationGain: About 250 feet on the lower-falls trail
/washington/snoqualmie/snoqualmie-falls.difficulty: Easy, with one steep climb back up from the lower viewpoint
/washington/snoqualmie/snoqualmie-falls.parking: Free lot across the street (sky bridge), paid lot next to the falls ($7 per hour), and a small lower lot ($7)
/washington/snoqualmie/snoqualmie-falls.fees: Admission is free; parking fees apply in the paid lots
/washington/snoqualmie/snoqualmie-falls.swimming: No; do not cross gates or railings to the river
/washington/snoqualmie/snoqualmie-falls.accessibility: Upper viewing area is wheelchair accessible; the lower-falls trail is not
/washington/snoqualmie/snoqualmie-falls.bestSeason: Late fall through spring for the biggest flow; open sunrise to sunset every day

/minnesota/mendota-heights/minnehaha-fal.hike: Short walk from the park's lots to the viewing areas above the falls
/minnesota/mendota-heights/minnehaha-fal.parking: A pay lot, a free lot and on-street pay kiosks; rates are posted at the pay stations
/minnesota/mendota-heights/minnehaha-fal.fees: No entry fee; pay parking in some lots
/minnesota/mendota-heights/minnehaha-fal.dogs: Allowed on leash; the off-leash area closes to off-leash use on Dec. 21, 2026
/minnesota/mendota-heights/minnehaha-fal.accessibility: Accessible restrooms and the Wabun universal access play area; parking is free for vehicles with disability plates or placards
sources: Minneapolis Park & Recreation Board: Minnehaha Regional Park

/oklahoma/davis/turner-falls.parking: Level 1 permit $25 a day, Level 2 $15, Level 3 free (admission still required)
/oklahoma/davis/turner-falls.fees: Per-person admission. Summer (May 1 to Sept. 30): $16 adults weekdays, $20 weekends. Winter (Oct. 1 to Apr. 30): $9 weekdays, $12 weekends. Under 5 free
/oklahoma/davis/turner-falls.dogs: No pets; only ADA service animals
/oklahoma/davis/turner-falls.swimming: Yes in the summer season, at your own risk and never after dark; children 12 and under must wear a Coast Guard approved life jacket. Swimming is closed in winter
/oklahoma/davis/turner-falls.bestSeason: May to September for swimming; closed Thanksgiving and Christmas Day

/california/burney/burney-falls.hike: The Falls Loop Trail is about 1 to 1.2 miles
/california/burney/burney-falls.fees: $10 day-use fee per vehicle; a summer reservation pilot ended Sept. 27, 2026
/california/burney/burney-falls.dogs: Only in parking lots, paved roads and campgrounds; not on trails or at the Lake Britton beach
/california/burney/burney-falls.swimming: Not in the falls pool; Lake Britton has a designated swimming beach
sources: California State Parks: McArthur-Burney Falls Memorial SP

/hawaii/hilo/rainbow-falls.hike: Paved path from the parking lot to the viewpoint
/hawaii/hilo/rainbow-falls.fees: Non-residents pay $5 per person plus $10 per vehicle (card only); Hawaii residents free. One payment also covers Boiling Pots
/hawaii/hilo/rainbow-falls.swimming: No; strong currents, slick rock and flash floods, and no lifeguards
/hawaii/hilo/rainbow-falls.accessibility: Viewpoint is reachable on a paved path, suitable for limited mobility
/hawaii/hilo/rainbow-falls.bestSeason: Morning visits for the rainbow in the mist; open 7 a.m. to 5:30 p.m. daily
sources: Hawaii Division of State Parks: Wailuku River State Park

/new-york/palenville/kaaterskill-falls.hike: 0.3 mile each way from Laurel House Road to the top viewing platform; about 0.7 mile each way to the lower pools
/new-york/palenville/kaaterskill-falls.elevationGain: About 100 feet to the platform; about 240 feet to the middle and lower falls
/new-york/palenville/kaaterskill-falls.difficulty: Easy to the platform; moderate with stairs to the lower falls
/new-york/palenville/kaaterskill-falls.parking: Use the Laurel House Road lot; roadside parking on Route 23A is prohibited
/new-york/palenville/kaaterskill-falls.swimming: No swimming or wading within 150 feet upstream of the falls; stay at least 6 feet from cliff edges

/georgia/cleveland/anna-ruby-falls.hike: Paved trail about 0.4 mile each way (0.8 mile round trip); the accessible Lion's Eye Trail is about 0.1 mile
/georgia/cleveland/anna-ruby-falls.fees: $6 per visitor age 16 and up; 15 and under free
/georgia/cleveland/anna-ruby-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash outdoors; not in the gift shop or restrooms
/georgia/cleveland/anna-ruby-falls.accessibility: Lion's Eye Trail is designed for accessibility; the main trail is paved but steep
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Anna Ruby Falls Recreation Area
FIND Outdoors: Anna Ruby Falls know before you go

/kentucky/whitley-city/cumberland-falls.parking: Free lots near the falls; they fill early on weekends and moonbow nights
/kentucky/whitley-city/cumberland-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash in outdoor areas and on trails
/kentucky/whitley-city/cumberland-falls.swimming: No swimming in the Cumberland River at the falls; the park has a seasonal pool
/kentucky/whitley-city/cumberland-falls.accessibility: A paved path reaches the upper viewing deck; lower platforms and trails have stairs and steep grades
/kentucky/whitley-city/cumberland-falls.bestSeason: Spring for flow; moonbow nights around the full moon draw crowds
sources: Kentucky Tourism: Moonbow Trail at Cumberland Falls

/pennsylvania/saw-creek/bushkill-falls.hike: Four color-coded trails: Green about 15 minutes, Yellow about 45 minutes, Blue about 1 hour 15 minutes, and Red (all eight falls) over 2 hours and nearly 2 miles
/pennsylvania/saw-creek/bushkill-falls.difficulty: Easy (Green) to strenuous (Red), with many stairs
/pennsylvania/saw-creek/bushkill-falls.fees: $24 adults, $22 seniors 62+ and active military, $12 ages 4 to 10, free 3 and under
/pennsylvania/saw-creek/bushkill-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash; owners must clean up
/pennsylvania/saw-creek/bushkill-falls.swimming: No swimming or wading for people or pets

/alabama/gadsden/noccalula-falls.hike: The Gorge Trail (included with admission) leads below and behind the falls; the separate Black Creek Trail is 1.7 miles
/alabama/gadsden/noccalula-falls.fees: $10 adults, $8 ages 4 to 12 and seniors 55+, free 3 and under
/alabama/gadsden/noccalula-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash in the park and campground; not on the train

/michigan/newberry/upper-falls.hike: Paved path of about 0.4 mile from the Upper Falls lot to the viewing platforms
/michigan/newberry/upper-falls.fees: Michigan Recreation Passport required per vehicle (non-residents $12 a day or $42 a year)
/michigan/newberry/upper-falls.dogs: Allowed on a 6-foot leash on trails and platforms
/michigan/newberry/upper-falls.accessibility: Accessible paved path and boardwalk to the brink viewpoint
sources: Michigan DNR: Tahquamenon Falls State Park

/north-carolina/franklin/dry-falls.hike: Paved trail of about 0.1 mile each way with stairs; the path goes behind the 75-foot falls
/north-carolina/franklin/dry-falls.parking: Small lot on US 64 about 2 miles west of Highlands; fills by midday
/north-carolina/franklin/dry-falls.fees: $3 per vehicle per day; a $15 annual pass also covers Whiteside Mountain and Whitewater Falls
/north-carolina/franklin/dry-falls.accessibility: An accessible walkway reaches an upper overlook
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Dry Falls Trail

/hawaii/maunawili/manoa-falls.hike: 0.8 mile each way (1.6 miles round trip) on a muddy rainforest trail
/hawaii/maunawili/manoa-falls.parking: Paid lot at the trailhead (about $7); do not park at Lyon Arboretum, where hikers are towed
/hawaii/maunawili/manoa-falls.swimming: No; the pool below the falls is closed to swimming and wading
sources: Hawaii DLNR Forestry & Wildlife: Oahu FAQ

/hawaii/wailua-homesteads/wailua-falls.hike: Roadside viewpoint at the end of Ma'alo Road; there is no authorized trail to the bottom
/hawaii/wailua-homesteads/wailua-falls.fees: Since Feb. 22, 2026, non-residents pay $5 per person (age 4+) plus $10 per vehicle, card only; Hawaii residents free
/hawaii/wailua-homesteads/wailua-falls.swimming: No; the route to the base is closed and posted no hiking
/hawaii/wailua-homesteads/wailua-falls.accessibility: Viewed from the roadside parking area
sources: Hawaii Division of State Parks: Wailua River State Park
DLNR visitor notice: new parking and entry fees (PDF)

/idaho/twin-falls/shoshone-falls.fees: $5 per vehicle while the ticket booth is open (from April 1 in 2026); $25 season pass
/idaho/twin-falls/shoshone-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash in Shoshone Falls Park; not on the Dierkes Lake lawn
/idaho/twin-falls/shoshone-falls.swimming: Not at the falls; swimming is at nearby Dierkes Lake
/idaho/twin-falls/shoshone-falls.bestSeason: April to June, during snowmelt; summer and fall flows are often low because of irrigation diversions
sources: City of Twin Falls: Shoshone Falls
City of Twin Falls: 2026 ticket booth reopening

/colorado/manitou-springs/helen-hunt-fal.hike: The falls are beside the visitor center lot; the Silver Cascade Falls trail continues about 0.3 to 0.7 mile out and back
/colorado/manitou-springs/helen-hunt-fal.elevationGain: Roughly 200 to 280 feet on the Silver Cascade trail
/colorado/manitou-springs/helen-hunt-fal.difficulty: Easy to the falls; steep and rocky beyond the bridge
/colorado/manitou-springs/helen-hunt-fal.parking: Free paved lot at the visitor center; fills early in summer
sources: City of Colorado Springs: North Cheyenne Canon Park
City of Colorado Springs: Helen Hunt Falls Visitor Center

/north-carolina/brevard/sliding-rock.fees: $6 per person, 5 and under free (staffed season)
/north-carolina/brevard/sliding-rock.dogs: Allowed on leash, but dogs may not slide
/north-carolina/brevard/sliding-rock.swimming: Yes: sliding and swimming, with lifeguards Memorial Day through Labor Day, 9 a.m. to 6 p.m.; no lifeguards or open restrooms the rest of the year
/north-carolina/brevard/sliding-rock.bestSeason: Memorial Day to Labor Day, when lifeguards are on duty
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Sliding Rock Recreation Area

/michigan/rogers-city/ocqueoc-falls.hike: Short paved path from the parking area
/michigan/rogers-city/ocqueoc-falls.fees: Michigan Recreation Passport required per vehicle
/michigan/rogers-city/ocqueoc-falls.accessibility: Billed by the Michigan DNR as a universally accessible waterfall: paved path, ramp to the river, accessible picnic areas and benches
sources: Michigan DNR news: Ocqueoc Falls has universal appeal

/wyoming/moose-wilson-road/mystic-falls.hike: 2.4 miles round trip on the Mystic Falls Trail; an optional switchback climb to an overlook of the Upper Geyser Basin adds 1.5 miles. Biscuit Basin's lot and boardwalk have been closed since the July 2024 hydrothermal explosion, so start from the Daisy Trail pullouts, which adds about half a mile each way
/wyoming/moose-wilson-road/mystic-falls.elevationGain: Modest to the falls; about 500 feet more if you climb to the overlook
/wyoming/moose-wilson-road/mystic-falls.difficulty: Rated moderately strenuous by the park
/wyoming/moose-wilson-road/mystic-falls.parking: Roadside pullouts on the Grand Loop Road about 0.25 mile south of Biscuit Basin while the Biscuit Basin lot is closed
/wyoming/moose-wilson-road/mystic-falls.fees: No trail fee; Yellowstone entrance fees apply
/wyoming/moose-wilson-road/mystic-falls.dogs: No; pets are not allowed on Yellowstone trails or boardwalks

/michigan/iron-river/bond-falls.hike: About a five-minute walk from the main lower lot on a paved path to a 600-foot boardwalk with six viewing spots; a loop trail climbs both banks to the cascades above
/michigan/iron-river/bond-falls.difficulty: Easy on the boardwalk; stairs and uneven ground on the upper loop
/michigan/iron-river/bond-falls.parking: Main lower lot off Scenic Overlook Drive (Recreation Passport required); free roadside parking near the Bond Falls Outpost at the top of the falls, which means stairs down to the viewing deck
/michigan/iron-river/bond-falls.fees: Michigan Recreation Passport required for vehicles in the main lot; a self-registration station is at the entrance. Walk-ins and cyclists do not need one
/michigan/iron-river/bond-falls.accessibility: Boardwalk and main viewing deck are wheelchair accessible from the lower lot; the upper roadside access is not
/michigan/iron-river/bond-falls.bestSeason: Vehicle access usually runs mid-May to mid-October; the trail stays open year-round but is not groomed for snow and ice
sources: Michigan DNR: Bond Falls Scenic Site
Michigan DNR: accessible trails and scenic sites

/arizona/grand-canyon-village/havasu-fal.hike: 10 miles one way from Hualapai Hilltop to the campground (8 miles to Supai Village, then 2 more); day hiking is not allowed
/arizona/grand-canyon-village/havasu-fal.difficulty: Strenuous desert backpacking trip; trails close when temperatures exceed 115 degrees
/arizona/grand-canyon-village/havasu-fal.parking: Hualapai Hilltop trailhead, at the end of Indian Highway 18; no services there
/arizona/grand-canyon-village/havasu-fal.fees: Reservation required for every visitor and every stay is 4 days and 3 nights. 2026 prices: campground $455 per person, lodge $2,277 per room for up to four
/arizona/grand-canyon-village/havasu-fal.dogs: No; pets, service animals and private horses are not allowed anywhere on the reservation

/utah/orem/bridal-veil-falls.hike: Normally about half a mile of the paved Provo River Parkway from parking to the base. Closed since an Oct. 23, 2026 rockslide: the trail from the Nunn's Park turnoff to the falls is shut through winter, with repairs planned for spring
/utah/orem/bridal-veil-falls.difficulty: Easy on the paved parkway; unofficial paths above the base are steep and dangerous
/utah/orem/bridal-veil-falls.parking: Lower lot and Nunn's Park off US-189; the upper overlook lot closes for winter on Nov. 1
/utah/orem/bridal-veil-falls.accessibility: The paved parkway is flat and works for wheelchairs and strollers when open
sources: Utah County Parks: Bridal Veil Falls
KSL: rockfall closes Bridal Veil Falls trail

/new-york/south-hill/ithaca-falls.hike: About 0.1 mile each way on gravel from Lake Street at East Falls Street; the falls are also visible from the Lake Street bridge
/new-york/south-hill/ithaca-falls.difficulty: Short, but the last stretch is rough and uneven
/new-york/south-hill/ithaca-falls.parking: Lake Street, with small lots near the corner of Lake and East Falls streets; TCAT bus stop Lake @ Falls
/new-york/south-hill/ithaca-falls.swimming: No; swimming in Fall Creek is illegal and the currents near the falls are deadly
/new-york/south-hill/ithaca-falls.accessibility: A flat path at the park entrance reaches a creek overlook; the path to the falls is rough
/new-york/south-hill/ithaca-falls.bestSeason: Open year-round; flow is loudest in spring

/washington/tanner/franklin-falls.hike: 2 miles round trip on Franklin Falls Trail 1036 to a 70-foot falls; in winter, when Denny Creek Road is gated, it is about 7 miles round trip from the Asahel Curtis Sno-Park
/washington/tanner/franklin-falls.difficulty: Easy family hike, with a rocky final descent to the pool
/washington/tanner/franklin-falls.parking: Franklin Falls Trailhead on Denny Creek Road (Forest Road 58)
/washington/tanner/franklin-falls.fees: Recreation pass required: $5 National Forest Day Pass, $30 Northwest Forest Pass, or an interagency pass. The Discover Pass is not valid

/california/carmel-valley-village/mcway-.hike: The McWay Falls Overlook Trail is 0.5 mile round trip, but it is closed for retaining-wall work with no reopening date posted
/california/carmel-valley-village/mcway-.parking: Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park day-use lot; limited spaces and no vehicles over 22 feet
/california/carmel-valley-village/mcway-.dogs: No; dogs are not allowed on park trails, only on leash in the paved parking area
sources: California State Parks: Julia Pfeiffer Burns trails
California State Parks: Julia Pfeiffer Burns day use

/washington/dayton/palouse-falls.hike: Short walks from the parking area to the main viewing area and gravel paths to the Fryxell Overlook; all trails into the canyon and to the base are permanently closed
/washington/dayton/palouse-falls.fees: Washington Discover Pass required ($10 day or $45 annual)
/washington/dayton/palouse-falls.swimming: No; the plunge pool is closed to the public
/washington/dayton/palouse-falls.accessibility: Paved interpretive path and viewing area are ADA accessible
sources: Washington State Parks: plan a Palouse Falls trip

/maryland/potomac/great-falls.hike: Great Falls Overlook boardwalk crosses Olmsted Island from the Great Falls Tavern area; Billy Goat Trail Section A is a separate rock scramble
/maryland/potomac/great-falls.parking: Great Falls Tavern area lots, inside the C&O Canal fee area
/maryland/potomac/great-falls.fees: Entrance pass required: $20 per vehicle, cashless (card only); annual and interagency passes accepted
/maryland/potomac/great-falls.dogs: Not on the Great Falls Overlook boardwalk or Billy Goat Trail Section A; allowed on a 6-foot leash on the towpath and Billy Goat Sections B and C
/maryland/potomac/great-falls.accessibility: Great Falls Overlook boardwalk is ADA accessible

/pennsylvania/birchwood-lakes/dingmans-f.hike: Closed to all visitors, including pedestrians, since May 12, 2025 for bridge and trail reconstruction, with no reopening date posted. When open, a boardwalk runs about 0.3 mile to near the base, then 0.1 mile of steep stairs
/pennsylvania/birchwood-lakes/dingmans-f.parking: Dingmans Falls Visitor Center lot; no buses or RVs on weekends and federal holidays
/pennsylvania/birchwood-lakes/dingmans-f.fees: No fee for the falls (the $10 Dingmans Access fee is for a separate river access)
/pennsylvania/birchwood-lakes/dingmans-f.dogs: No; only trained service dogs on the trail and in the visitor center
/pennsylvania/birchwood-lakes/dingmans-f.accessibility: When open, the boardwalk is wheelchair and stroller accessible to the lower viewpoint; the stairs to the base are not

/oregon/troutdale/latourell-falls.hike: Lower falls viewpoint is a few steps from the lot; the Latourell Falls Loop is 2.4 miles and passes Upper Latourell Falls
/oregon/troutdale/latourell-falls.elevationGain: About 600 feet on the full loop
/oregon/troutdale/latourell-falls.difficulty: Easy to the lower viewpoint; moderate on the loop
/oregon/troutdale/latourell-falls.parking: Guy W. Talbot State Park lot on the Historic Columbia River Highway
/oregon/troutdale/latourell-falls.fees: Oregon State Parks day-use parking permit required since March 30, 2026: $10 for Oregon residents, $12 for nonresidents
/oregon/troutdale/latourell-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet
/oregon/troutdale/latourell-falls.accessibility: The full loop is rocky and not wheelchair accessible
sources: Friends of the Columbia Gorge: Latourell Falls Loop
Oregon State Parks: day-use parking permits

/tennessee/dodson-branch/cummins-falls.hike: The 0.35-mile Falls Overlook Trail needs no permit; reaching the base means a steep, slippery descent and wading up the Blackburn Fork gorge
/tennessee/dodson-branch/cummins-falls.difficulty: Easy to the overlook; strenuous into the gorge
/tennessee/dodson-branch/cummins-falls.fees: Gorge Access Permit required for the base and swimming area, bought online in advance; the overlook is free
/tennessee/dodson-branch/cummins-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash, but the gorge route is not recommended for pets
/tennessee/dodson-branch/cummins-falls.swimming: Yes, in the gorge with a Gorge Access Permit, in fair weather only; it closes quickly for flash flooding. Children 5 and under should not go, and those 12 and under need a life jacket
sources: Tennessee State Parks: Gorge Access Permits

/tennessee/spencer/fall-creek-falls.hike: Fall Creek Falls Overlook is a paved path from its parking area; the Base of Falls Trail is 0.35 mile one way
/tennessee/spencer/fall-creek-falls.difficulty: Easy at the overlook; the base trail is difficult and rocky, with a steep climb back
/tennessee/spencer/fall-creek-falls.accessibility: The overlook has accessible parking and a paved path
sources: Tennessee State Parks: Fall Creek Falls hiking
Tennessee State Parks: Fall Creek Falls accessibility

/alabama/fort-payne/de-soto-falls.hike: Short walk from the DeSoto Falls Picnic Area; the main overlook is down about 50 concrete stairs
/alabama/fort-payne/de-soto-falls.parking: DeSoto Falls Picnic Area near Mentone; limited spaces, open daylight to dusk
/alabama/fort-payne/de-soto-falls.swimming: Only above the A. A. Miller Dam and in designated West Fork areas; not on the cascade or within 50 feet of the falls
/alabama/fort-payne/de-soto-falls.accessibility: The dam and upper falls area are accessible; the main overlook requires stairs
sources: Alabama State Parks: DeSoto Falls Picnic Area

/massachusetts/sheffield/bash-bish-falls.hike: About 0.7 mile round trip from the Falls Road lot in Massachusetts; the route from the New York side (Taconic State Park) is about 1.5 miles round trip and gentler
/massachusetts/sheffield/bash-bish-falls.difficulty: Steep and rugged from the Massachusetts lot
/massachusetts/sheffield/bash-bish-falls.parking: Free lot on Falls Road (about 24 cars); roadside parking is prohibited
/massachusetts/sheffield/bash-bish-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash at all times
/massachusetts/sheffield/bash-bish-falls.swimming: No; swimming, diving and entering the water are prohibited
sources: Mass.gov: Bash Bish Falls State Park

/ohio/boston-heights/brandywine-falls.hike: About 0.3 mile round trip on the upper boardwalk; the lower head-on viewing deck is down about 80 steps
/ohio/boston-heights/brandywine-falls.parking: Brandywine Falls lot (about 90 spaces, with accessible spaces) on Stanford Road; no overflow parking and it often fills by mid-morning on nice days
/ohio/boston-heights/brandywine-falls.fees: No fee; Cuyahoga Valley National Park has no entrance fee
/ohio/boston-heights/brandywine-falls.accessibility: Upper boardwalk overlook is wheelchair accessible

/michigan/munising/munising-falls.hike: Normally an 800-foot paved trail from the lot to the viewing platform. Closed with no alternate access after a washout; a rebuilt, fully accessible route is expected by the end of 2027
/michigan/munising/munising-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash when the trail is open

/hawaii/pupukea/waimea-falls.hike: About 3/4 mile each way on a paved path through the Waimea Valley gardens
/hawaii/pupukea/waimea-falls.fees: Admission: $26 adults, $20 seniors and students, $18 ages 4 to 12; Hawaii residents and military $10, $8 and $6
/hawaii/pupukea/waimea-falls.swimming: Only when lifeguards say conditions are safe; free life jackets are required. Call (808) 638-7766 to check that day

/oklahoma/sulphur/little-niagara-falls.fees: No entrance or parking fee at Chickasaw National Recreation Area; lots can fill on summer weekends
/oklahoma/sulphur/little-niagara-falls.dogs: Allowed on a 6-foot leash in nearby picnic areas, but not in the water at Little Niagara or the other named falls
/oklahoma/sulphur/little-niagara-falls.swimming: Yes, in Travertine Creek from Little Niagara downstream; swimming and wading upstream of it are prohibited

/oregon/deschutes-river-woods/tumalo-fal.hike: The viewpoint is a few steps from the lot; a short trail climbs to an upper viewing platform. In winter Forest Road 4603 closes to cars, adding roughly 2.5 miles each way from Skyliners Sno-Park
/oregon/deschutes-river-woods/tumalo-fal.parking: Tumalo Falls Day Use Area; limited spaces and vehicles over 27 feet are restricted
/oregon/deschutes-river-woods/tumalo-fal.fees: $5 per vehicle per day, or a Northwest Forest Pass or interagency pass
/oregon/deschutes-river-woods/tumalo-fal.dogs: Allowed on leash on the Tumalo Falls Trail; not allowed in the Bend Municipal Watershed or on the Bridge Creek Trail
sources: USFS: Tumalo Falls Day Use Area

/idaho/ashton/upper-mesa-falls.hike: Short accessible boardwalk and trail from the visitor center to Upper Mesa Falls overlooks; Mesa Falls Nature Trail is about 1 mile one way to a Lower Mesa Falls overlook (when open)
/idaho/ashton/upper-mesa-falls.difficulty: Easy to the Upper Falls overlooks; easy on the Nature Trail
/idaho/ashton/upper-mesa-falls.parking: Lots at the Upper Mesa Falls visitor center and at Lower Mesa Falls Grandview overlook on Mesa Falls Scenic Byway (Highway 47)
/idaho/ashton/upper-mesa-falls.fees: $5 per vehicle per day when open ($1 for motorcycles, bicycles, horses and hikers; $25 for tour buses). As of fall 2026 both Upper and Lower Mesa Falls were closed for construction, with reopening aimed for spring 2027
/idaho/ashton/upper-mesa-falls.dogs: Leashed pets welcome when the site is open (per Visit Idaho recreation guidance)
/idaho/ashton/upper-mesa-falls.swimming: Stay on boardwalks and overlooks; do not climb down toward the river
/idaho/ashton/upper-mesa-falls.accessibility: Accessible trail and boardwalk from the visitor center to Upper Falls overlooks (when open); trail paving and boardwalk replacement were part of the 2026–27 work
/idaho/ashton/upper-mesa-falls.bestSeason: Summer; Scenic Byway 47 is typically closed to vehicles in winter and groomed for snowmobiles
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Mesa Falls Visitor Center
U.S. Forest Service: Closures at Mesa Falls (Sept. 16, 2026)

/georgia/dawsonville/amicalola-falls.hike: West Ridge Falls Access Trail is about 0.3 mile to falls overlooks without stairs; the climb beside the falls uses about 604 stairs from the Reflection Pool to the top; East Ridge Loop options are about 2 miles
/georgia/dawsonville/amicalola-falls.elevationGain: About 600–780 feet for the full stair/loop climbs; minimal on the West Ridge Access Trail
/georgia/dawsonville/amicalola-falls.difficulty: Easy on the West Ridge Access Trail; strenuous on the 604-stair climb
/georgia/dawsonville/amicalola-falls.parking: Lots near the Reflection Pool and visitor center; $10 daily ParkPass required for vehicles
/georgia/dawsonville/amicalola-falls.fees: $10 per vehicle per day Georgia State Park Pass, or $70 annual ParkPass
/georgia/dawsonville/amicalola-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet on trails and in the campground; not in the lodge or Hike Inn
/georgia/dawsonville/amicalola-falls.swimming: Not at the falls; stay off wet rock and out of the water beside the falls
/georgia/dawsonville/amicalola-falls.accessibility: West Ridge Falls Access Trail is a short, recycled-tire-surface path to overlooks with no stairs; accessible parking and restrooms near the falls lot
/georgia/dawsonville/amicalola-falls.bestSeason: Spring for strongest flow; late October for typical peak fall color in north Georgia
sources: Georgia State Parks: Amicalola Falls State Park & Lodge

/georgia/blairsville/helton-creek-falls.hike: Helton Creek Falls Trail is an easy 0.2 mile hike with abrupt grade changes to observation decks for the upper and lower falls
/georgia/blairsville/helton-creek-falls.difficulty: Easy, with short steep and uneven sections
/georgia/blairsville/helton-creek-falls.parking: Small pullout on Helton Creek Road about 2.2 miles from US 19/129; fills on summer weekends, with roadside overflow
/georgia/blairsville/helton-creek-falls.dogs: Leashed pets allowed in developed recreation sites; pets (except service animals) are not allowed in swimming areas on the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest
/georgia/blairsville/helton-creek-falls.swimming: People commonly swim at the base; Forest Service warns against climbing on or jumping from waterfalls and playing in water above falls
/georgia/blairsville/helton-creek-falls.bestSeason: Open year-round; strongest flow after rain and in spring
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Helton Creek Falls
U.S. Forest Service: Waterfall dangers alert

/virginia/nellysford/crabtree-falls.hike: Moderate 2.7-mile Forest Service trail past five major cascades totaling about 1,200 feet of drop; first overlook is a short paved walk from the lot
/virginia/nellysford/crabtree-falls.elevationGain: About 1,000–1,120 feet for the full climb to the upper overlook
/virginia/nellysford/crabtree-falls.difficulty: Easy to the first overlook; moderate for the full trail
/virginia/nellysford/crabtree-falls.parking: Upper and lower lots at Crabtree Falls Day Use Area off SR 56; vault toilets at the trailhead
/virginia/nellysford/crabtree-falls.fees: $3 per vehicle per day; America the Beautiful and George Washington & Jefferson National Forests seasonal day-use passes accepted
/virginia/nellysford/crabtree-falls.dogs: Must be leashed at all times on a leash no longer than 6 feet in the recreation area
/virginia/nellysford/crabtree-falls.swimming: No; stay on the trail. Leaving the trail onto wet rock has caused numerous fatalities
/virginia/nellysford/crabtree-falls.accessibility: First waterfall overlook is universally accessible via a short paved trail
/virginia/nellysford/crabtree-falls.bestSeason: Open year-round, sunrise to sunset; best after rain; lots fill on nice weekends
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Crabtree Falls Day Use Area

/new-mexico/carlsbad/sitting-bull-falls.hike: ADA-accessible path from the parking lot to the falls viewing area; additional hiking trails in the recreation area
/new-mexico/carlsbad/sitting-bull-falls.difficulty: Easy to the main viewing area
/new-mexico/carlsbad/sitting-bull-falls.parking: Day-use lot at the end of Forest Road 276 / County Road 409 west of Carlsbad; picnic sites, restrooms and potable water on site
/new-mexico/carlsbad/sitting-bull-falls.fees: $10 per vehicle per day or $25 per multi-passenger vehicle; New Mexico Enchantment Pass and interagency passes accepted
/new-mexico/carlsbad/sitting-bull-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash in developed recreation sites; pets are not allowed in swimming areas under Forest Service developed-site rules
/new-mexico/carlsbad/sitting-bull-falls.swimming: Spring-fed pool below the falls is commonly used for wading when water is present; stay off wet rock around the cliffs
/new-mexico/carlsbad/sitting-bull-falls.accessibility: ADA-accessible path to the falls viewing area
/new-mexico/carlsbad/sitting-bull-falls.bestSeason: Open daily 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m.; entry gate closes by 3:30 p.m.; cooler months are more comfortable in the Chihuahuan Desert
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Sitting Bull Falls Recreation Area

/georgia/cleveland/dukes-creek-falls.hike: Moderate day-hike trail from the Russell-Brasstown Scenic Highway recreation area to Dukes Creek Falls overlooks
/georgia/cleveland/dukes-creek-falls.parking: Day-use lot at 1699 Richard Russell Hwy (Hwy 348) near Helen; day-use only, no overnight parking
/georgia/cleveland/dukes-creek-falls.fees: $4 per vehicle per day; America the Beautiful passes accepted; pay by credit card, fee envelope, or Recreation.gov Scan & Pay
/georgia/cleveland/dukes-creek-falls.dogs: Leashed pets allowed in developed recreation sites
/georgia/cleveland/dukes-creek-falls.swimming: Forest Service waterfall-danger alert covers this site; stay on trail and observation areas
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Dukes Creek Falls Recreation Area

/tennessee/baxter/burgess-falls.hike: River Trail / Service Road loop of about 1.5 miles round trip past a series of falls on Falling Water River
/tennessee/baxter/burgess-falls.parking: Park lots; capacity can be limited during construction or peak weekends—use designated spaces only
/tennessee/baxter/burgess-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash in day-use areas
/tennessee/baxter/burgess-falls.swimming: No designated swim area; swimming is not permitted at the falls
/tennessee/baxter/burgess-falls.accessibility: Some paved paths and overlooks; confirm current accessible routes with the park during construction periods
/tennessee/baxter/burgess-falls.bestSeason: Spring for strongest flow; park open during daylight hours
sources: Tennessee State Parks: Burgess Falls hiking

/tennessee/rockwood/ozone-falls.hike: Short trail from the Highway 70 pullout to the overlook and a steep, rocky path toward the plunge pool (about 0.3 mile one way to the base area)
/tennessee/rockwood/ozone-falls.difficulty: Easy to the overlook; difficult and slippery to the base
/tennessee/rockwood/ozone-falls.parking: Roadside pullout / small lot along US 70 at Ozone Falls State Natural Area; free
/tennessee/rockwood/ozone-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash; terrain to the base is poor for most dogs
/tennessee/rockwood/ozone-falls.swimming: Plunge pool is sometimes used for swimming; no lifeguards, cold water and currents possible
/tennessee/rockwood/ozone-falls.bestSeason: Open sunrise to sunset; strongest after rain
sources: Tennessee Department of Environment & Conservation: Ozone Falls State Natural Area

/oregon/oakridge/salt-creek-falls-lane.hike: Wheelchair-accessible observation platform about 50 yards from the parking lot; short paved Salt Creek Falls Trail #3673 loop along the rim; steep stair trail to the base is not wheelchair accessible
/oregon/oakridge/salt-creek-falls-lane.difficulty: Easy to the overlook; moderate with stairs to the base
/oregon/oakridge/salt-creek-falls-lane.parking: Lot off Highway 58 / Forest Road 5893 east of Oakridge; overflow at Salt Creek Sno-Park 0.4 mile up the road; do not park on Highway 58
/oregon/oakridge/salt-creek-falls-lane.fees: $5 per vehicle per day, or Northwest Forest Pass / interagency recreation pass
/oregon/oakridge/salt-creek-falls-lane.dogs: On a leash no longer than 6 feet, or otherwise under physical control, in developed recreation sites
/oregon/oakridge/salt-creek-falls-lane.swimming: No; viewing from overlooks and trails only
/oregon/oakridge/salt-creek-falls-lane.accessibility: Observation platform is wheelchair accessible with railings that accommodate wheelchair sight lines
/oregon/oakridge/salt-creek-falls-lane.bestSeason: Late spring through fall; lot not maintained for snow and ice in winter (access then via Sno-Park on foot)
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Salt Creek Falls Observation Site

/new-hampshire/tamworth/sabbaday-falls.hike: Easy gravel trail from the paved Kancamagus Highway lot; about a 15-minute walk with a stone staircase beside the falls
/new-hampshire/tamworth/sabbaday-falls.parking: Paved lot on the Kancamagus Highway about 15 miles west of Conway; fills quickly on summer weekends
/new-hampshire/tamworth/sabbaday-falls.fees: Recreation day-use pass required spring through fall ($5 day pass, White Mountain annual, or interagency pass); no fee in winter when the site is not fee-operated
/new-hampshire/tamworth/sabbaday-falls.bestSeason: Late spring through fall for easiest road access; winter visits possible but expect ice
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Sabbaday Falls Observation Site
U.S. Forest Service: White Mountain National Forest passes

/michigan/munising/miners-falls.hike: 0.6 mile one way on a gently rolling gravel and dirt path to two viewing platforms; 64 steps down to the lower platform
/michigan/munising/miners-falls.parking: Lot about 4 miles north of Alger County Road H-58 off Miners Castle Road (H-11)
/michigan/munising/miners-falls.fees: Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore entrance pass required ($25 per private vehicle for 7 days, or $45 annual park pass); America the Beautiful pass accepted. Michigan Recreation Passport is not a substitute
/michigan/munising/miners-falls.dogs: Leashed pets (6-foot leash) allowed on the trail and viewing platforms
/michigan/munising/miners-falls.bestSeason: Spring for wildflowers and strong flow; summer for easiest road access

/california/bolinas/alamere-falls.hike: No park-sanctioned shortcut. Recommended routes go to Wildcat Campground then about 1.1 miles south on Wildcat Beach at low tide: about 13 miles round trip minimum (roughly 6.5 miles one way from Palomarin via Coast Trail, or longer from Bear Valley or Five Brooks)
/california/bolinas/alamere-falls.elevationGain: Varies by trailhead; Five Brooks / Stewart Trail climbs over Inverness Ridge (about 1,300 feet)
/california/bolinas/alamere-falls.parking: Palomarin (~75 spaces; fills early and may close when full), Bear Valley trailhead gravel lot (~210 spaces), or Five Brooks (~50 spaces). No parking or entrance fee
/california/bolinas/alamere-falls.fees: No parking or entrance fee at Point Reyes National Seashore
/california/bolinas/alamere-falls.dogs: Dogs and other pets prohibited on trails to Alamere Falls (service dogs excepted)
/california/bolinas/alamere-falls.swimming: Ocean swimming not recommended due to surf and currents; Bass Lake swimming rules are separate—check current NPS guidance
/california/bolinas/alamere-falls.bestSeason: Summer and fall usually have more beach sand for the Wildcat Beach approach; always check tide and surf forecasts before the beach walk

/oregon/sisters/sahalie-falls.hike: Viewpoint a short walk from the Sahalie Falls lot; Waterfalls Loop Trail / McKenzie River Trail connects Sahalie and Koosah Falls (about 0.4–2.5 miles depending on out-and-back vs. full loop)
/oregon/sisters/sahalie-falls.difficulty: Easy to the viewpoint; easy to moderate for the loop
/oregon/sisters/sahalie-falls.parking: Lot on Highway 126 about 0.5 mile north of the Koosah Falls turnoff; do not park on the highway. Lots are not maintained for snow and ice in winter
/oregon/sisters/sahalie-falls.dogs: On a leash no longer than 6 feet, or otherwise under physical control, in developed recreation sites
/oregon/sisters/sahalie-falls.swimming: No; powerful river and falls—view from trails and platforms
/oregon/sisters/sahalie-falls.accessibility: Sahalie Falls viewpoint near the east-side parking area is a short, relatively level walk suitable for many strollers and wheelchairs in dry conditions
/oregon/sisters/sahalie-falls.bestSeason: Spring for peak flow; day use 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Sahalie and Koosah Falls

/north-carolina/franklin/bridal-veil-fal.hike: Roadside stop on US 64 in the Cullasaja Gorge; short walk along the old roadbed that passes behind the falls
/north-carolina/franklin/bridal-veil-fal.parking: Small roadside pull-offs beside US 64; limited spaces
/north-carolina/franklin/bridal-veil-fal.dogs: Allowed; keep leashed near the highway and wet rock
/north-carolina/franklin/bridal-veil-fal.bestSeason: Year-round when US 64 is open; strongest after rain

/hawaii/pepeekeo/akaka-falls.hike: ʻAkaka Falls Loop Trail is a 0.4-mile paved loop with steps to viewpoints of Kahuna Falls and 442-foot ʻAkaka Falls; a shorter spur left at the first junction reaches ʻAkaka Falls alone
/hawaii/pepeekeo/akaka-falls.parking: Lot at the end of ʻAkaka Falls Road (Highway 220), 3.6 miles southwest of Honomu
/hawaii/pepeekeo/akaka-falls.fees: Credit card only. Non-residents: $5 per person (ages 4+) plus $10 per non-commercial vehicle. Hawaiʻi residents free for entry and parking with valid ID. Children 3 and under free
/hawaii/pepeekeo/akaka-falls.accessibility: Not wheelchair accessible due to multiple steps
/hawaii/pepeekeo/akaka-falls.bestSeason: Open daily 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.; pay before arrival when possible due to limited cell reception
sources: Hawaiʻi Division of State Parks: ʻAkaka Falls State Park

/colorado/alamosa-east/zapata-falls.hike: About 0.5 mile one way from the day-use lot to the falls; final approach requires carefully walking upstream in a rocky creek slot
/colorado/alamosa-east/zapata-falls.difficulty: Easy to moderate; cold water and slippery rock on the final stretch
/colorado/alamosa-east/zapata-falls.parking: BLM Zapata Falls Day Use Area lot south of Great Sand Dunes; free, fills on weekends
/colorado/alamosa-east/zapata-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash and under control
/colorado/alamosa-east/zapata-falls.swimming: Wading to view the falls is common; swimming is not the purpose of the site—water is cold and the slot is confined
/colorado/alamosa-east/zapata-falls.bestSeason: Late spring through early fall; snow and ice linger at the falls into spring
sources: BLM: Zapata Falls Day Use Area

/idaho/marsing/jump-creek-falls.hike: Short canyon walk from the lower lot to the falls, about 0.25 mile one way
/idaho/marsing/jump-creek-falls.parking: Lower lot for the falls trail at Jump Creek Recreation Site southwest of Marsing; open 6 a.m. to 9 p.m.
/idaho/marsing/jump-creek-falls.swimming: Swimming and wading at the base of the falls are common when water levels allow
/idaho/marsing/jump-creek-falls.bestSeason: Spring for stronger flow; summer for swimming (water can be low by late summer)

/west-virginia/hinton/sandstone-falls.hike: Accessible wooden boardwalk about 1/4 mile along Sandstone Falls; optional Island Loop Trail adds about another 1/4 mile off the boardwalk
/west-virginia/hinton/sandstone-falls.parking: Sandstone Falls day-use lot on New River Road / WV-26 south of Hinton; includes accessible spaces next to the boardwalk entrance
/west-virginia/hinton/sandstone-falls.fees: No activity fee; New River Gorge National Park & Preserve does not charge an entrance fee here
/west-virginia/hinton/sandstone-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash 6 feet or shorter; pick up after pets
/west-virginia/hinton/sandstone-falls.swimming: Viewing from the boardwalk; the New River is powerful—stay on designated paths
/west-virginia/hinton/sandstone-falls.accessibility: Boardwalk is accessible; two handicapped parking spaces next to the boardwalk start
sources: NPS: Stroll on the Sandstone Boardwalk

/oregon/cascade-locks/horsetail-falls.hike: Roadside view of lower Horsetail Falls across the Historic Columbia River Highway; Horsetail Falls Trail #438 is a short, steep hike that passes behind Upper Horsetail Falls (Ponytail Falls) and connects to Oneonta Trail #424
/oregon/cascade-locks/horsetail-falls.difficulty: Easy for the roadside view; moderate and steep for Trail #438, with cliff exposure
/oregon/cascade-locks/horsetail-falls.parking: Lot on the north side of the Historic Columbia River Highway about 2.75 miles east of Multnomah Falls; includes accessible parking (you must cross the highway to the viewing area)
/oregon/cascade-locks/horsetail-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash on Forest Service trails
/oregon/cascade-locks/horsetail-falls.accessibility: Roadside viewing area and picnic tables after crossing the highway; trail beyond is steep and not accessible
/oregon/cascade-locks/horsetail-falls.bestSeason: Winter and spring for strongest Gorge flow; day use sunrise to sunset
sources: U.S. Forest Service: Horsetail Falls Trailhead & Day Use
U.S. Forest Service: Horsetail Falls Trail #438

/virginia/covington/falling-spring-falls.hike: Short paved walk from the parking area to the overlook; no trail beyond the overlook
/virginia/covington/falling-spring-falls.parking: Roadside lot on US 220 about 5 miles north of Covington; picnic area on site
/virginia/covington/falling-spring-falls.fees: Free; managed by Virginia State Parks (Douthat State Park)
/virginia/covington/falling-spring-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash at the overlook area
/virginia/covington/falling-spring-falls.swimming: No; no trespassing beyond the overlook (strictly enforced)
/virginia/covington/falling-spring-falls.accessibility: Paved walk from parking to overlook
/virginia/covington/falling-spring-falls.bestSeason: Year-round when US 220 is open; strongest after rain

/pennsylvania/towamensing-trails/hawk-fa.hike: Hawk Falls Trail is about 1.2 miles round trip through rhododendron to a roughly 25-foot waterfall on Hawk Run
/pennsylvania/towamensing-trails/hawk-fa.parking: Dedicated lots on PA Route 534 at Hickory Run State Park; can fill early on weekends
/pennsylvania/towamensing-trails/hawk-fa.fees: No day-use or parking fee at Hickory Run State Park
/pennsylvania/towamensing-trails/hawk-fa.dogs: Allowed on leash and attended at all times
/pennsylvania/towamensing-trails/hawk-fa.swimming: No designated swim area at Hawk Falls; enjoy from the trail and creek banks without climbing wet rock
/pennsylvania/towamensing-trails/hawk-fa.bestSeason: Spring and after rain; park open sunrise to sunset
sources: Pennsylvania DCNR: Hickory Run State Park hiking
Pennsylvania DCNR: Hickory Run State Park

/washington/eatonville/narada-falls.hike: Upper roadside viewpoint of the top of the falls; steep 0.2-mile one-way trail (0.4 mile round trip) with about 200 feet of descent to the lower overlook of the full 168-foot falls
/washington/eatonville/narada-falls.elevationGain: About 200 feet of descent/ascent on the lower viewpoint trail
/washington/eatonville/narada-falls.difficulty: Easy for the upper viewpoint; moderate and slippery for the lower trail
/washington/eatonville/narada-falls.parking: Narada Falls parking and rest area on the road to Paradise, about 17 miles east of the Nisqually Entrance; picnic tables and accessible restrooms
/washington/eatonville/narada-falls.fees: Mount Rainier National Park entrance fee ($30 per private vehicle for up to 7 days, or annual park / America the Beautiful pass)
/washington/eatonville/narada-falls.dogs: Pets are not allowed on park trails, including the trail to the lower viewpoint; pets may stay in developed parking areas under control
/washington/eatonville/narada-falls.accessibility: Accessible restroom at the parking area; lower viewpoint trail is steep, wet and not wheelchair accessible
/washington/eatonville/narada-falls.bestSeason: Summer and early fall for snow-free lower trail; upper pullout is open year-round but the lower trail is hazardous when snow-covered

/new-york/trumansburg/taughannock-falls.hike: Gorge Trail is about 0.75 mile one way (about 1.5 miles round trip) on a wide, relatively flat path to the 215-foot falls; rim trails offer overlook views
/new-york/trumansburg/taughannock-falls.parking: Lots at the upper (overlook / trails) and lower (lake / beach) entrances off Taughannock Blvd in Trumansburg
/new-york/trumansburg/taughannock-falls.fees: $10 per vehicle entrance fee collected daily sunup to sundown; Empire Pass accepted
/new-york/trumansburg/taughannock-falls.dogs: Maximum two pets in day-use areas; leash no more than 6 feet; not permitted in playgrounds, buildings, boardwalks, pools or guarded beaches (service animals excepted)
/new-york/trumansburg/taughannock-falls.swimming: Not in the gorge. Guarded Cayuga Lake beach swimming in 2026: June 26 through Labor Day, 11 a.m. to 7 p.m.
/new-york/trumansburg/taughannock-falls.accessibility: Gorge Trail is relatively flat and is among the more accessible Finger Lakes gorge walks; contact the park for current accessible-route details
/new-york/trumansburg/taughannock-falls.bestSeason: Spring for strongest flow; park open dawn to dusk year-round
sources: NYS Parks: Taughannock Falls State Park

/california/rancho-cucamonga/bonita-fall.hike: About 1.5 miles round trip on an unmarked route up the South Fork Lytle Creek wash, then a short side path to the lower falls
/california/rancho-cucamonga/bonita-fall.elevationGain: Roughly 350 to 450 feet, mostly near the falls
/california/rancho-cucamonga/bonita-fall.difficulty: Easy to moderate: rocky creek wash, stream crossings and uneven footing; no signed trail
/california/rancho-cucamonga/bonita-fall.parking: Bonita Falls day-use area and turnouts along Lytle Creek Road in San Bernardino National Forest, about a mile past the Lytle Creek ranger station; fills early on summer weekends
/california/rancho-cucamonga/bonita-fall.fees: San Bernardino National Forest Adventure Pass for parking ($5 day or $30 annual) or America the Beautiful pass; no separate trail permit
/california/rancho-cucamonga/bonita-fall.dogs: Allowed on leash in developed recreation areas and on trails under national forest rules
/california/rancho-cucamonga/bonita-fall.swimming: No official swimming rule found; rockfall hazard is serious near the cliffs
/california/rancho-cucamonga/bonita-fall.accessibility: Not wheelchair accessible; the wash route is rocky and uneven
/california/rancho-cucamonga/bonita-fall.bestSeason: Winter and spring after rain, when flow is strongest; summer weekends fill parking early
sources: USDA Forest Service: San Bernardino National Forest
USDA Forest Service: dogs on national forests

/california/yosemite-valley/bridalveil-f.hike: 0.5 mile round trip on a paved trail from the Bridalveil Fall parking area (about 20 minutes); an alternate approach from Southside Drive roadside parking adds about 0.25 mile each way
/california/yosemite-valley/bridalveil-f.parking: Bridalveil Fall Parking Area off Wawona Road / Southside Drive; fills quickly in summer. Overflow roadside parking a few hundred yards east on Southside Drive
/california/yosemite-valley/bridalveil-f.fees: Yosemite National Park entrance fee ($35 per private vehicle for up to 7 days, or annual park / America the Beautiful pass)
/california/yosemite-valley/bridalveil-f.dogs: Leashed pets are allowed on the paved Bridalveil Fall trails
/california/yosemite-valley/bridalveil-f.swimming: Do not enter Bridalveil Creek at the viewpoint; rocks are slick and the creek is cold and swift. Parkwide swimming rules apply elsewhere
/california/yosemite-valley/bridalveil-f.accessibility: A wheelchair-accessible viewing platform sits about halfway up the trail from the main lot; the final viewpoint has a steeper grade and is not wheelchair accessible. Accessible family restroom at the parking area
/california/yosemite-valley/bridalveil-f.bestSeason: Spring and early summer for peak flow and heavy spray; flows year-round with a lighter, windswept look later in the year

/arizona/flagstaff/grand-falls.hike: Historically a short walk from informal roadside parking to overlooks of the Little Colorado River falls; no maintained public trail while closed
/arizona/flagstaff/grand-falls.difficulty: Not applicable while closed to the public
/arizona/flagstaff/grand-falls.parking: Access road has been barricaded by local residents; do not attempt to park or drive in
/arizona/flagstaff/grand-falls.fees: Closed to the public. No permit currently authorizes a visit for non-residents
/arizona/flagstaff/grand-falls.dogs: Not applicable; site is closed. Navajo Nation parks generally restrict pets
/arizona/flagstaff/grand-falls.accessibility: Not verified; site is closed to the public
/arizona/flagstaff/grand-falls.bestSeason: Not open. Historically strongest flow in spring snowmelt and monsoon season on the Little Colorado River
sources: Navajo Nation Parks & Recreation: rules & regulations
Arizona Republic: Grand Falls closed by Navajo communities (March 2023)

/arkansas/marshall/falling-water-falls.hike: Roadside viewpoint from Forest Road 1205; a short, steep informal path leads to the base of the falls
/arkansas/marshall/falling-water-falls.difficulty: Easy for the roadside view; moderate and steep if descending to the base
/arkansas/marshall/falling-water-falls.parking: Gravel pull-offs along Forest Road 1205 in Ozark-St. Francis National Forest / Richland Creek area
/arkansas/marshall/falling-water-falls.fees: No day-use or entrance fee listed for this roadside stop; forest road conditions vary
/arkansas/marshall/falling-water-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash under national forest rules
/arkansas/marshall/falling-water-falls.swimming: Visitors wade the creek pools; no separate agency swimming rule found for this pull-off—use caution on slick rock
/arkansas/marshall/falling-water-falls.accessibility: Roadside view only for those who cannot manage the steep informal path to the base
/arkansas/marshall/falling-water-falls.bestSeason: Winter and spring for strongest flow; gravel forest roads can be rough after rain
sources: USDA Forest Service: Richland Creek Wilderness
University of Arkansas: Northwest Arkansas waterfall viewing guide

/new-york/pulaski/salmon-river-falls.hike: Accessible Falls Trail is 0.2 mile one way from the Falls Road parking area to the overlook. Optional steep Gorge Trail (about 600 feet) and River Bed Trail drop into the gorge when open
/new-york/pulaski/salmon-river-falls.difficulty: Easy on the accessible overlook trail; strenuous on the Gorge and River Bed trails
/new-york/pulaski/salmon-river-falls.parking: Falls Road parking area about one mile up Falls Road east of County Route 22 (Orwell / Altmar area)
/new-york/pulaski/salmon-river-falls.dogs: Keep pets under control and on a leash when other visitors are present
/new-york/pulaski/salmon-river-falls.swimming: No. Public access is prohibited in the restricted area around the cliff face and plunge pool, including swimming and wading
/new-york/pulaski/salmon-river-falls.accessibility: Falls Trail is wheelchair accessible: 0.2 mile, gentle grade (max about 10%), firm compacted stone, minimum 3-foot width
/new-york/pulaski/salmon-river-falls.bestSeason: Year-round for the overlook; Gorge and River Bed trails are closed Nov. 15 to May 1 and during high water (ice climbers may use the Gorge Trail in winter with daily registration)
sources: NYSDEC: Salmon River Falls Unique Area

/colorado/pagosa-springs/treasure-falls.hike: Treasure Falls Trail 563 is 0.4 mile one way (about 0.8 mile round trip) from the paved US-160 lot to viewpoints and a mist deck at the roughly 100-foot falls
/colorado/pagosa-springs/treasure-falls.difficulty: Easy to moderate short climb; Forest Service describes it as a short accessible interpretive trail
/colorado/pagosa-springs/treasure-falls.parking: Paved lot directly off US Highway 160 about 16 miles east of Pagosa Springs; often crowded at peak times
/colorado/pagosa-springs/treasure-falls.fees: No fee listed for this day-use trailhead
/colorado/pagosa-springs/treasure-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash under national forest rules
/colorado/pagosa-springs/treasure-falls.swimming: No swimming area; stay on the trail and viewing decks
/colorado/pagosa-springs/treasure-falls.accessibility: Forest Service lists it as an accessible interpretive trail with a paved parking area; expect some uphill grade to the falls
/colorado/pagosa-springs/treasure-falls.bestSeason: Late spring through early fall for snow-free footing; trail can be icy in winter
sources: USDA Forest Service: Treasure Falls Trail

/north-carolina/brevard/triple-falls.hike: About 1 mile round trip from the Hooker Falls Access Area on Staton Road, or about 2.2 miles round trip from the High Falls / visitor center parking
/north-carolina/brevard/triple-falls.difficulty: Moderate: short distance with a steep section and stairs at the overlook
/north-carolina/brevard/triple-falls.parking: Hooker Falls Access Area or High Falls Access Area; free, first come, first served. Lots fill early—N.C. Forest Service suggests before 9 a.m. or after about 4–5 p.m.
/north-carolina/brevard/triple-falls.swimming: No swimming or wading within 300 feet upstream of waterfalls; no climbing, jumping or diving at waterfalls. Hooker Falls downstream is the usual swimming spot when conditions allow
/north-carolina/brevard/triple-falls.accessibility: The Triple Falls trail is not wheelchair accessible. Limited-mobility visitors may request a free vehicle-access permit to High Falls (advance request)
/north-carolina/brevard/triple-falls.bestSeason: Spring for flow; weekdays or early/late hours to avoid parking closures when lots fill
sources: N.C. Forest Service: DuPont State Recreational Forest FAQ

/tennessee/tullahoma/machine-falls.hike: Machine Falls Trail in Short Springs State Natural Area; loop options with Adams / Busby Falls are commonly about 2 to 3 miles round trip depending on route
/tennessee/tullahoma/machine-falls.difficulty: Moderate: descent into the gorge with rocky, rooty footing
/tennessee/tullahoma/machine-falls.parking: Small lot on Short Springs Road opposite the water tower northeast of Tullahoma; extremely limited (about a dozen spaces). Do not park outside designated spots—if full, return later
/tennessee/tullahoma/machine-falls.fees: Free public access; no entry fee listed
/tennessee/tullahoma/machine-falls.swimming: No swimming facilities; cascades and wet rock make wading hazardous
/tennessee/tullahoma/machine-falls.accessibility: Not wheelchair accessible; steep gorge trails
/tennessee/tullahoma/machine-falls.bestSeason: Spring for wildflowers and strongest seeps; winter–spring for flow. Weekdays recommended for parking
sources: Tennessee Division of Natural Areas: Short Springs

/washington/eatonville/little-mashel-fal.hike: About 5 miles round trip via UW Pack Forest roads/trails to Lower, Middle and Upper (Tom Tom) Falls, or a shorter approach on the Bud Blancher Trail; both meet near the falls
/washington/eatonville/little-mashel-fal.difficulty: Moderate; footing near the falls can be slick
/washington/eatonville/little-mashel-fal.parking: Pack Forest entrance off Highway 7 near Eatonville (limited spaces at the trailhead plus overflow near administration buildings), or Bud Blancher Trail parking in Eatonville
/washington/eatonville/little-mashel-fal.fees: No parking pass or entry fee
/washington/eatonville/little-mashel-fal.swimming: Not recommended; slick rock and strong current at the falls. Fatalities have occurred near Middle Falls
/washington/eatonville/little-mashel-fal.accessibility: Not wheelchair accessible; crushed-rock roads and steep side trails
/washington/eatonville/little-mashel-fal.bestSeason: Late fall through spring for strong flow; avoid peak flood when spray and footing are worst
sources: Washington Trails Association: Little Mashel Falls - Pack Forest

/california/yosemite-valley/vernal-fall.hike: Mist Trail to the top of Vernal Fall is 2.4 miles round trip from Happy Isles with about 1,000 feet of elevation gain; continue to Nevada Fall for a longer day
/california/yosemite-valley/vernal-fall.elevationGain: About 1,000 feet to the top of Vernal Fall
/california/yosemite-valley/vernal-fall.difficulty: Moderate to strenuous: steep granite stairs, wet and slippery in high spray
/california/yosemite-valley/vernal-fall.parking: Use Yosemite Valley day-use parking and the free Valley shuttle to Happy Isles (Stop 16); trailhead parking is limited
/california/yosemite-valley/vernal-fall.fees: Yosemite National Park entrance fee ($35 per private vehicle for up to 7 days, or annual park / America the Beautiful pass)
/california/yosemite-valley/vernal-fall.dogs: Pets are not allowed on the Mist Trail or John Muir Trail
/california/yosemite-valley/vernal-fall.swimming: Swimming and wading are prohibited at Emerald Pool and the Silver Apron above Vernal Fall; stay out of the river near the falls
/california/yosemite-valley/vernal-fall.accessibility: Not wheelchair accessible; steep stairs and uneven granite
/california/yosemite-valley/vernal-fall.bestSeason: Late spring and early summer for full Mist Trail spray; winter ice can close or make stairs hazardous
sources: NPS: Vernal Fall and Nevada Fall Trails

/pennsylvania/dunbar/cucumber-falls.hike: Short stair/path from the Cucumber Falls parking area on Ohiopyle Road to the falls, or about 1 mile one way on Meadow Run Trail from other park lots
/pennsylvania/dunbar/cucumber-falls.difficulty: Easy to moderate; stairs and rocky footing near the falls
/pennsylvania/dunbar/cucumber-falls.parking: Cucumber Falls lot on Ohiopyle Road in Ohiopyle State Park, or Meadow Run Trail parking for the longer approach
/pennsylvania/dunbar/cucumber-falls.fees: No Pennsylvania state park entrance fee for day use
/pennsylvania/dunbar/cucumber-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash and attended on park trails
/pennsylvania/dunbar/cucumber-falls.swimming: Not a designated swimming area; currents and slick rock are hazardous
/pennsylvania/dunbar/cucumber-falls.accessibility: Cucumber Falls access is not listed as ADA; other park features (including parts of the Great Allegheny Passage) are accessible
/pennsylvania/dunbar/cucumber-falls.bestSeason: Spring for strongest flow; trail can flood in high water
sources: PA DCNR: Hiking at Ohiopyle State Park
PA DCNR: Ohiopyle State Park accessibility

/indiana/cloverdale/upper-cataract-falls.hike: Short trails within Cataract Falls State Recreation Area link the upper falls viewpoints; commonly under 1 mile round trip for the main overlooks
/indiana/cloverdale/upper-cataract-falls.parking: Lots inside Cataract Falls SRA (Cagles Mill Lake / Lieber SRA complex) near Cloverdale
/indiana/cloverdale/upper-cataract-falls.fees: Indiana State Park entrance fee: $7 in-state / $9–$15 out-of-state per vehicle depending on current DNR rates (verify at gate)
/indiana/cloverdale/upper-cataract-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet and attended
/indiana/cloverdale/upper-cataract-falls.swimming: No swimming along the creek or at the waterfalls
/indiana/cloverdale/upper-cataract-falls.accessibility: Some paved overlook areas; confirm current accessible routes with Indiana DNR
/indiana/cloverdale/upper-cataract-falls.bestSeason: Spring for strongest Mill Creek flow
sources: Indiana DNR: Cagles Mill Lake (Lieber and Cataract Falls SRA)
Indiana DNR: State park entrance fees

/north-carolina/brevard/hooker-falls.hike: About 0.5 to 0.8 mile round trip on an easy, mostly flat trail from the Hooker Falls Access Area to the base of the falls
/north-carolina/brevard/hooker-falls.parking: Hooker Falls Access Area on Staton Road; free lots fill early on weekends
/north-carolina/brevard/hooker-falls.swimming: Swimming is allowed in the pool below Hooker Falls when conditions are safe; never swim or wade above the falls or within 300 feet upstream of any DuPont waterfall
/north-carolina/brevard/hooker-falls.accessibility: Relatively flat approach compared with Triple and High Falls, but not a certified wheelchair route; surfaces can be uneven
/north-carolina/brevard/hooker-falls.bestSeason: Late spring through summer for swimming; year-round for viewing
sources: N.C. Forest Service: DuPont State Recreational Forest FAQ
Friends of DuPont Forest: Hooker Falls

/vermont/morristown/moss-glen-falls.hike: About 0.5 mile round trip from the small lot at the end of Moss Glen Falls Road (Stowe area) to the falls
/vermont/morristown/moss-glen-falls.parking: Small free lot at the end of Moss Glen Falls Road; do not block the bus turnaround. Fills quickly on summer weekends
/vermont/morristown/moss-glen-falls.swimming: People wade the pool below the falls; cold water and slick rock—no lifeguard
/vermont/morristown/moss-glen-falls.accessibility: Short path but not a certified accessible route
/vermont/morristown/moss-glen-falls.bestSeason: Spring for strongest flow; summer for swimming weather

/pennsylvania/milford-pike/raymondskill-.hike: 0.3-mile loop / out-and-back with about 178 feet of elevation change between upper and lower viewing areas; a seasonal spur leads about 0.25 mile one way to Raymondskill Creek (not to the base of the falls)
/pennsylvania/milford-pike/raymondskill-.difficulty: Easy to moderate: short but steep and uneven
/pennsylvania/milford-pike/raymondskill-.parking: Upper and lower lots on Raymondskill Road in Delaware Water Gap National Recreation Area; upper lot closed early January to mid-April. Restrooms at the upper lot when open
/pennsylvania/milford-pike/raymondskill-.fees: No entrance or parking fee at Raymondskill Falls
/pennsylvania/milford-pike/raymondskill-.dogs: Pets are not permitted on the trail (trained service animals excepted)
/pennsylvania/milford-pike/raymondskill-.swimming: Swimming and wading are not permitted within 50 feet upstream of waterfalls or in the waterfalls themselves
/pennsylvania/milford-pike/raymondskill-.accessibility: Trail is steep and uneven; not wheelchair accessible
/pennsylvania/milford-pike/raymondskill-.bestSeason: Spring for strongest flow; summer shuttle may operate—check NPS for current operations
sources: NPS: Delaware Water Gap fees & passes
NPS: Pets in Delaware Water Gap

/new-york/niagara-falls/american-falls.hike: Paved park paths and overlooks at Prospect Point and nearby viewpoints; Observation Tower and other ticketed attractions are optional
/new-york/niagara-falls/american-falls.parking: Niagara Falls State Park Lots 1–3; rates change by season (Lot 1/2 commonly about $10/day in peak periods; Lot 3 has free days/seasonal free periods—check current park parking page)
/new-york/niagara-falls/american-falls.fees: Park grounds and main American Falls viewpoints are free; parking and ticketed attractions (Observation Tower, Cave of the Winds, Maid of the Mist) cost extra
/new-york/niagara-falls/american-falls.dogs: Leashed pets (6 feet or less) allowed on green space and footpaths with falls views; not in buildings, attractions or boardwalks
/new-york/niagara-falls/american-falls.swimming: No swimming in the Niagara River gorge
/new-york/niagara-falls/american-falls.accessibility: Park pathways and many viewpoints are ADA accessible; confirm elevator/tower access for Observation Tower tickets
/new-york/niagara-falls/american-falls.bestSeason: Year-round; illumination and ice make winter distinctive, summer has longest hours and biggest crowds
sources: Niagara Falls State Park: pet-friendly policies
NYS Parks: Niagara Falls State Park

/michigan/k-i-sawyer-air-force-base/laug.hike: About 1 mile round trip (0.5 mile each way) on a natural-surface trail to three viewing platforms
/michigan/k-i-sawyer-air-force-base/laug.difficulty: Easy to the upper platform; moderate with many stairs to the lower platforms (about 20 stairs to middle, about 137 to lower)
/michigan/k-i-sawyer-air-force-base/laug.parking: Trailhead lot reached by a seasonal dirt road that can be muddy and is not plowed in winter
/michigan/k-i-sawyer-air-force-base/laug.fees: Michigan Recreation Passport required for vehicles ($12 day or $42 annual for out-of-state; in-state passport via vehicle registration)
/michigan/k-i-sawyer-air-force-base/laug.dogs: Allowed on a 6-foot leash under immediate control; pack out waste
/michigan/k-i-sawyer-air-force-base/laug.swimming: No designated swimming; gorge and stairs are for viewing
/michigan/k-i-sawyer-air-force-base/laug.accessibility: Upper platform is stair-free but the trail is natural surface; middle and lower platforms require stairs. Accessible vault toilet at the trailhead
/michigan/k-i-sawyer-air-force-base/laug.bestSeason: Late spring through fall when the access road is firm; winter access is unreliable
sources: Michigan DNR: Laughing Whitefish Falls State Park

/indiana/cloverdale/lower-cataract-falls.hike: Short trails within Cataract Falls State Recreation Area connect the lower falls viewpoints; typically a short walk from nearby parking
/indiana/cloverdale/lower-cataract-falls.parking: Lots inside Cataract Falls SRA near the lower falls
/indiana/cloverdale/lower-cataract-falls.fees: Indiana State Park entrance fee: $7 in-state / out-of-state rates higher (verify current DNR gate fees)
/indiana/cloverdale/lower-cataract-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet and attended
/indiana/cloverdale/lower-cataract-falls.swimming: No swimming along the creek or at the waterfalls
/indiana/cloverdale/lower-cataract-falls.accessibility: Some paved areas near overlooks; confirm current accessible routes with Indiana DNR
/indiana/cloverdale/lower-cataract-falls.bestSeason: Spring for strongest Mill Creek flow
sources: Indiana DNR: Cagles Mill Lake (Lieber and Cataract Falls SRA)
Indiana DNR: State park entrance fees

/tennessee/tracy-city/foster-falls.hike: Overlook about 0.4 mile round trip; steep rocky Base Trail about 0.6 mile round trip down to the plunge pool
/tennessee/tracy-city/foster-falls.difficulty: Easy to the overlook; moderate to strenuous on the Base Trail
/tennessee/tracy-city/foster-falls.parking: Fiery Gizzard South / Foster Falls trailhead at 498 Foster Falls Road, Sequatchie; restrooms and picnic area at the trailhead
/tennessee/tracy-city/foster-falls.fees: Tennessee State Parks charge no day-use entrance fee
/tennessee/tracy-city/foster-falls.swimming: Swimming is allowed in the plunge pool when conditions allow; no lifeguard, depth and current vary
/tennessee/tracy-city/foster-falls.accessibility: Overlook path is the easier option; Base Trail is steep and not wheelchair accessible. Park hours typically 8 a.m. to 30 minutes before sunset
/tennessee/tracy-city/foster-falls.bestSeason: Late spring through early fall for swimming weather; spring for stronger flow
sources: Tennessee State Parks: Fiery Gizzard State Park
Tennessee State Parks: FAQ (no day-use entrance fee)

/washington/gold-bar/deception-falls.hike: About 0.5-mile interpretive loop (Trail 1078) with bridges and viewing platforms; a platform near the parking area views the falls
/washington/gold-bar/deception-falls.parking: Paved day-use lot at US Highway 2 milepost 56 (north side), Mount Baker-Snoqualmie National Forest
/washington/gold-bar/deception-falls.fees: No fees required for this site
/washington/gold-bar/deception-falls.swimming: No; viewing platforms and picnic area only
/washington/gold-bar/deception-falls.accessibility: Accessible covered picnic shelter; short loop includes wooden platforms and bridges—confirm current accessible segments with the Skykomish Ranger Station
/washington/gold-bar/deception-falls.bestSeason: Spring runoff for strongest flow; open year-round when Highway 2 is open
sources: USDA Forest Service: Deception Falls Picnic Area and Interpretive Trail

/oregon/lyons/abiqua-falls.hike: About 0.8 mile round trip from the usual high-clearance parking near the canyon rim, with a steep, rocky, rope-assisted descent into the amphitheater
/oregon/lyons/abiqua-falls.elevationGain: Roughly 200 to 300 feet of steep descent/ascent
/oregon/lyons/abiqua-falls.difficulty: Moderate to strenuous because of the scramble; not a built trail
/oregon/lyons/abiqua-falls.parking: Limited roadside / spur parking reached via Crooked Finger Road; high-clearance recommended. Lower-clearance vehicles often park at Crooked Finger OHV Area and walk farther
/oregon/lyons/abiqua-falls.fees: No parking permit or day-use fee listed for the current informal access (Oregon State Parks has approved a future recreation-area purchase—rules may change)
/oregon/lyons/abiqua-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash, but the steep rope section is difficult for most dogs
/oregon/lyons/abiqua-falls.swimming: People wade the pool at the base; cold water and slick rock—no lifeguard
/oregon/lyons/abiqua-falls.bestSeason: Late spring through early fall for drier roads and safer rock; avoid after heavy rain when the descent is slick
sources: Oregon Hikers Field Guide: Abiqua Falls Hike

/north-carolina/tryon/pearsons-falls.hike: Short preserve trail from the parking area to the falls inside Pearson's Falls & Glen (Thermal Belt area near Saluda / Tryon)
/north-carolina/tryon/pearsons-falls.parking: On-site parking at Pearson's Falls & Glen; reservation required for entry
/north-carolina/tryon/pearsons-falls.fees: $10 per person ages 13+; ages 12 and under free (confirm current rates when booking)
/north-carolina/tryon/pearsons-falls.swimming: No swimming; viewing only from preserve paths
/north-carolina/tryon/pearsons-falls.accessibility: Contact the preserve for current accessible-path details before visiting
/north-carolina/tryon/pearsons-falls.bestSeason: Spring for flowers and flow; book ahead on weekends
sources: Pearson's Falls & Glen: plan your visit

/michigan/lanse/canyon-falls.hike: About 0.5 mile one way on the Canyon Gorge Trail from Canyon Falls Roadside Park to the main falls; longer gorge walks continue beyond
/michigan/lanse/canyon-falls.parking: Canyon Falls Roadside Park day-use lot on US-41 near L'Anse; spaces for cars and RVs
/michigan/lanse/canyon-falls.fees: Free; no Michigan Recreation Passport required at this MDOT roadside park
/michigan/lanse/canyon-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash of 6 feet or less and attended
/michigan/lanse/canyon-falls.swimming: Not a swimming area; stay behind railings at overlooks
/michigan/lanse/canyon-falls.accessibility: Short natural-surface trail; not a certified wheelchair route to the gorge overlooks
/michigan/lanse/canyon-falls.bestSeason: Late spring through fall; roadside park is day-use
sources: Outdoor Michigan: Canyon Falls Roadside Park

/washington/port-angeles/marymere-falls.hike: 0.9 mile one way (1.8 miles round trip) from Storm King Ranger Station on Lake Crescent; also reachable from Lake Crescent Lodge
/washington/port-angeles/marymere-falls.difficulty: Easy, with stairs up to the upper and lower viewpoints at the falls
/washington/port-angeles/marymere-falls.dogs: Not allowed; Olympic National Park permits pets only on a few trails, such as the Spruce Railroad Trail
/washington/port-angeles/marymere-falls.accessibility: The first 0.5 mile is accessible; stairs lead to the waterfall viewpoints
/washington/port-angeles/marymere-falls.bestSeason: Year-round; flow is strongest during the wet season from fall through spring

/north-carolina/spruce-pine/linville-fal.hike: All trails start at the Linville Falls Visitor Center (Blue Ridge Parkway): Erwins View Trail 1.6 miles round trip with four overlooks; Plunge Basin Overlook 1 mile round trip; Linville Gorge Trail to the base 1.4 miles round trip
/north-carolina/spruce-pine/linville-fal.difficulty: Erwins View is moderate with a strenuous stretch near Chimney View; the Plunge Basin and Gorge trails are strenuous
/north-carolina/spruce-pine/linville-fal.parking: Linville Falls Visitor Center lot off the Blue Ridge Parkway
/north-carolina/spruce-pine/linville-fal.fees: No fee; the Blue Ridge Parkway has no entrance fee
/north-carolina/spruce-pine/linville-fal.swimming: No; swimming in the Linville River and climbing on the rocks is not allowed
/north-carolina/spruce-pine/linville-fal.bestSeason: Spring for wildflowers and high water; October for fall color

/north-carolina/spruce-pine/crabtree-fal.hike: 2.5-mile loop from Blue Ridge Parkway milepost 339.5 to the base of the 60-foot falls; you can return the way you came or continue past the top of the falls to close the loop
/north-carolina/spruce-pine/crabtree-fal.parking: Crabtree Falls area at Parkway milepost 339.5, which also has a seasonal campground and picnic area
/north-carolina/spruce-pine/crabtree-fal.fees: No fee to hike; the Blue Ridge Parkway has no entrance fee (camping is extra)
/north-carolina/spruce-pine/crabtree-fal.bestSeason: Late spring through fall; facilities are seasonal, and pink turtlehead blooms along the trail in late summer

/missouri/winona/rocky-falls.hike: 0.4-mile trail from the parking area on Route NN; the falls and pool are right by the picnic area
/missouri/winona/rocky-falls.parking: Free lot at the picnic area and trailhead on State Highway NN, off Route H east of Eminence and Winona
/missouri/winona/rocky-falls.fees: No fee; Ozark National Scenic Riverways has no entrance fee
/missouri/winona/rocky-falls.swimming: Yes, the pool below the falls is a popular spring and summer swimming hole; rocks are slippery
/missouri/winona/rocky-falls.accessibility: Trail is 0.4 mile with slopes under 5% and a firm surface, plus benches, an accessible restroom and accessible parking
/missouri/winona/rocky-falls.bestSeason: Spring for the strongest flow; summer for swimming. Open year-round

/new-jersey/paterson/great-falls.hike: Overlooks are a short walk from the park lot at 72 McBride Avenue Extension in Paterson
/new-jersey/paterson/great-falls.parking: Free national park lot at 72 McBride Avenue Extension (closes after dark, reopens 7:45 to 8:45 a.m.); nearby municipal garages charge
/new-jersey/paterson/great-falls.dogs: Allowed on a six-foot non-retractable leash
/new-jersey/paterson/great-falls.bestSeason: Spring and after heavy rain; some paths and facilities close in winter. Grounds are open 24 hours, but daylight is best
sources: NPS: Paterson Great Falls Basic Information

/tennessee/centerville/jackson-falls.hike: Paved 900-foot trail from the Natchez Trace Parkway rest area at milepost 404.7 down to the falls (go right from the restrooms)
/tennessee/centerville/jackson-falls.difficulty: Short but steep; you climb back up on the return. Do not climb on the falls, the rock is very slick
/tennessee/centerville/jackson-falls.parking: Jackson Falls rest area at Natchez Trace Parkway milepost 404.7
/tennessee/centerville/jackson-falls.fees: No fee; the Natchez Trace Parkway has no entrance fee
sources: NPS: Trails in the Northern Section of the Parkway

/tennessee/mount-pleasant/stillhouse-hol.hike: The falls are about 2/3 mile along the Stillhouse Hollow Falls trail; the full loop is about 1.2 miles
/tennessee/mount-pleasant/stillhouse-hol.parking: Small lot on US-43 about 3 miles northeast of Summertown; parking is extremely limited and you may not park outside marked spaces, so go on a weekday or early
/tennessee/mount-pleasant/stillhouse-hol.bestSeason: Spring for wildflowers and strongest flow
sources: TDEC: Stillhouse Hollow Falls State Natural Area

/tennessee/sparta/virgin-falls.hike: About 8.5 miles round trip (4.3 miles one way) on the Virgin Falls Trail in Scott's Gulf
/tennessee/sparta/virgin-falls.difficulty: Strenuous; roughly 1,000 feet of descent and climb back out. Allow most of a day
sources: TDEC: Virgin Falls State Natural Area
Tennessee State Parks: Scott's Gulf hiking
