/michigan/munising/wagner-falls.hike: 0.1-mile packed-gravel trail and boardwalk to an observation platform
/michigan/munising/wagner-falls.parking: Small lot for 8 to 10 cars on M-94 about 0.3 mile west of M-28, 1.5 miles south of Munising
/michigan/munising/wagner-falls.fees: Michigan Recreation Passport required for vehicle entry
/michigan/munising/wagner-falls.accessibility: Packed gravel and boardwalk with a few steps to the platform; no restrooms or water on site
/michigan/munising/wagner-falls.bestSeason: Spring melt for the most water; early October for fall color
sources: Michigan DNR: Wagner Falls Scenic Site

/new-hampshire/gorham/glen-ellis-falls.hike: Short trail from the Glen Ellis Falls lot on the west side of NH-16, through a tunnel under the highway to the 66-foot falls
/new-hampshire/gorham/glen-ellis-falls.difficulty: Short but involves more than 150 stone steps down to the base, which you climb back up
/new-hampshire/gorham/glen-ellis-falls.parking: Glen Ellis Scenic Area lot on the west side of NH-16 in Pinkham Notch; no restrooms or drinking water
/new-hampshire/gorham/glen-ellis-falls.fees: White Mountain National Forest recreation fee charged

/california/palm-springs/tahquitz-falls.hike: About 1.8 miles round trip from the Tahquitz Canyon Visitor Center, 500 W Mesquite Ave, Palm Springs
/california/palm-springs/tahquitz-falls.difficulty: Desert canyon trail; water is required to go on the trail
/california/palm-springs/tahquitz-falls.fees: Admission $15 adults, $7 ages 6 to 12, free for U.S. military with ID; tickets at the visitor center. Ranger-led hikes are included
/california/palm-springs/tahquitz-falls.bestSeason: Winter and spring after rain. Open 7:30 a.m. to 5 p.m. daily Oct. 1 to July 5 (Fridays to Sundays only in summer); last hikers start at 3:30 p.m.
sources: Tahquitz Canyon (Agua Caliente): Admission and Hours

/massachusetts/royalston/doane-falls.hike: Half-mile trail down the west side of Lawrence Brook past a series of drops; part of the Tully Trail
/massachusetts/royalston/doane-falls.parking: Main lot on Athol Road holds 3 cars; a lower lot on Doane Hill Road serves the accessible trail
/massachusetts/royalston/doane-falls.fees: Free; open daily sunrise to sunset
/massachusetts/royalston/doane-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash at all times
/massachusetts/royalston/doane-falls.swimming: No; swimming, diving and wading are banned after fatalities and serious injuries, and access to the water is prohibited
/massachusetts/royalston/doane-falls.accessibility: An accessible trail of about 0.15 mile runs from the lower lot on Doane Hill Road to the lower falls

/massachusetts/royalston/royalston-falls.hike: Enter on the marked Tully Trail from Route 32 and descend to a granite gorge with a 45-foot falls; the reservation is also on the New England National Scenic Trail
/massachusetts/royalston/royalston-falls.difficulty: Strenuous and very slippery in places; not recommended for children under 6
/massachusetts/royalston/royalston-falls.parking: Lot on Route 32, 1.7 miles north of the end of Route 68; not plowed in winter
/massachusetts/royalston/royalston-falls.fees: Free; open daily sunrise to sunset
/massachusetts/royalston/royalston-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash at all times

/massachusetts/becket/glendale-falls.hike: A quarter-mile trail leads down along the falls to the bottom, where the property ends; do not continue downstream onto private land
/massachusetts/becket/glendale-falls.parking: Lot for about 7 cars on Clark Wright Road, Middlefield, 0.4 mile from East River Road
/massachusetts/becket/glendale-falls.fees: Free; open daily sunrise to sunset
/massachusetts/becket/glendale-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash at all times
/massachusetts/becket/glendale-falls.bestSeason: Spring, when Glendale Brook runs high

/connecticut/moodus/chapman-falls.parking: Devil's Hopyard State Park, 366 Hopyard Rd., East Haddam; buses seating 30 or more are not allowed
/connecticut/moodus/chapman-falls.fees: No fee; open daily 8 a.m. to sunset
/connecticut/moodus/chapman-falls.dogs: Allowed on leash in picnic areas and on trails; not in the campground
sources: CT State Parks: Devil's Hopyard State Park

/ohio/peninsula/blue-hen-falls.hike: About 3 miles round trip on the Buckeye Trail from the Boston Mill Visitor Center / Boston Trailhead, including a road crossing
/ohio/peninsula/blue-hen-falls.parking: Boston Mill Visitor Center or Boston Trailhead; parking along the road is prohibited
/ohio/peninsula/blue-hen-falls.fees: No fee; Cuyahoga Valley National Park has no entrance fee
sources: NPS: Hike to Blue Hen Falls from Boston

/california/mammoth-lakes/rainbow-falls.hike: About 1.5 miles one way (3 miles round trip) from the Rainbow Falls Trailhead in Devils Postpile National Monument
/california/mammoth-lakes/rainbow-falls.fees: During shuttle season most visitors must ride the Reds Meadow shuttle, which charges a fare; check NPS for current rates and road status
/california/mammoth-lakes/rainbow-falls.bestSeason: Summer to early fall, when the Reds Meadow road and shuttle are running
sources: NPS: Devils Postpile Fees and Passes

/wyoming/cody/upper-falls-of-the-yellows.hike: The Brink of the Upper Falls is a short walk from its own parking area off the Grand Loop Road to a fenced overlook at the top of the 109-foot falls
/wyoming/cody/upper-falls-of-the-yellows.fees: Yellowstone National Park entrance fee required
/wyoming/cody/upper-falls-of-the-yellows.bestSeason: Late spring and early summer for peak snowmelt flow; park roads are seasonal
sources: NPS: Grand Canyon of the Yellowstone

/georgia/toccoa/toccoa-falls.fees: $2 admission, paid inside the Gate Cottage Gift Shop. Hours Monday to Friday 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., Saturday and Sunday noon to 4 p.m. (may change for holidays or campus events)
sources: University of Toccoa Falls: Visiting Toccoa Falls

/virginia/stanley/dark-hollow-falls.hike: 1.4-mile round trip: 0.75 mile down to the falls from the Dark Hollow Falls parking area (Skyline Drive mile 50.7), then back up the same way
/virginia/stanley/dark-hollow-falls.difficulty: Moderate (NPS): short but very steep and rocky; the climb back up is the hard part
/virginia/stanley/dark-hollow-falls.parking: Dark Hollow Falls parking area at Skyline Drive mile 50.7
/virginia/stanley/dark-hollow-falls.fees: Shenandoah National Park entrance pass required: $30 per private vehicle for 7 days, $15 per person on foot or bike; cashless (card only); annual and interagency passes accepted
/virginia/stanley/dark-hollow-falls.dogs: Not allowed on this trail; NPS suggests the Rose River Loop from Fishers Gap instead

/virginia/stanley/rose-river-falls.hike: 4-mile circuit from Fishers Gap parking area (Skyline Drive mile 49.4) on the Skyland-Big Meadows Horse Trail and blue-blazed Rose River Loop Trail past the 67-foot falls
/virginia/stanley/rose-river-falls.difficulty: Moderate (NPS); steep, rocky section past cascades on the return
/virginia/stanley/rose-river-falls.parking: Fishers Gap parking area at Skyline Drive mile 49.4
/virginia/stanley/rose-river-falls.fees: Shenandoah National Park entrance pass required: $30 per private vehicle for 7 days, $15 per person on foot or bike; cashless (card only); annual and interagency passes accepted
/virginia/stanley/rose-river-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet

/virginia/stanley/upper-whiteoak-falls.hike: 4.6-mile round trip from the Whiteoak Canyon parking area (Skyline Drive mile 42.6) to a rocky ledge with a view of the upper falls, about 2.3 miles in
/virginia/stanley/upper-whiteoak-falls.parking: Whiteoak Canyon parking area at Skyline Drive mile 42.6
/virginia/stanley/upper-whiteoak-falls.fees: Shenandoah National Park entrance pass required: $30 per private vehicle for 7 days, $15 per person on foot or bike; cashless (card only); annual and interagency passes accepted
/virginia/stanley/upper-whiteoak-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet

/virginia/stanley/lower-whiteoak-falls.hike: 2-mile round trip from the Whiteoak Canyon boundary parking area on Route 600, keeping right at the Cedar Run Trail junction to the base of the lower falls
/virginia/stanley/lower-whiteoak-falls.parking: Whiteoak Canyon boundary trailhead lot at the end of Route 600 (outside Skyline Drive)
/virginia/stanley/lower-whiteoak-falls.fees: Shenandoah National Park entrance pass required: $30 per private vehicle for 7 days, $15 per person on foot or bike; cashless (card only); annual and interagency passes accepted; passes are sold at the Whiteoak Canyon lower trailhead
/virginia/stanley/lower-whiteoak-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet
/virginia/stanley/lower-whiteoak-falls.accessibility: Trail does not meet ADA accessibility guidelines

/virginia/stanardsville/south-river-fall.hike: 3.3-mile circuit from just below the South River Picnic Grounds comfort station (Skyline Drive mile 62.7) to an observation point and the base of the 83-foot falls, with one stream crossing
/virginia/stanardsville/south-river-fall.parking: South River Picnic Grounds at Skyline Drive mile 62.7
/virginia/stanardsville/south-river-fall.fees: Shenandoah National Park entrance pass required: $30 per private vehicle for 7 days, $15 per person on foot or bike; cashless (card only); annual and interagency passes accepted
/virginia/stanardsville/south-river-fall.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet

/virginia/washington/overall-run-falls.hike: 5.1-mile round trip from the Mathews Arm Campground registration parking area via Traces Trail, Mathews Arm Trail and Tuscarora-Overall Run Trail to views of the 93-foot falls, the park's tallest; about 1 mile longer from Skyline Drive mile 21 when the campground is closed
/virginia/washington/overall-run-falls.parking: Mathews Arm Campground registration parking area (mile 22.2); Appalachian Trail parking at mile 21 when the campground is closed
/virginia/washington/overall-run-falls.fees: Shenandoah National Park entrance pass required: $30 per private vehicle for 7 days, $15 per person on foot or bike; cashless (card only); annual and interagency passes accepted
/virginia/washington/overall-run-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet
/virginia/washington/overall-run-falls.bestSeason: After plentiful rain; NPS notes the falls may have minimal to no flow otherwise

/maryland/thurmont/cunningham-falls.hike: Lower Trail is 1/2 mile each way from the William Houck Area lake to the 78-foot falls; the rougher Cliff Trail (3/4 mile) makes a 1.5-mile round trip; a separate 1/4-mile Boardwalk Trail reaches the base
/maryland/thurmont/cunningham-falls.difficulty: Lower Trail easy to moderate; Cliff Trail strenuous over rock outcrops
/maryland/thurmont/cunningham-falls.parking: William Houck Area day-use lot, with overflow at the South Beach and North Beach lots; the Boardwalk Trail lot is only for vehicles with a disability placard
/maryland/thurmont/cunningham-falls.fees: Houck Area day use: Maryland residents $3 and out-of-state $5 per vehicle off-season; per person ($3 to $7) from Memorial Day weekend through Labor Day
/maryland/thurmont/cunningham-falls.dogs: Leashed pets welcome on the Lower Trail
/maryland/thurmont/cunningham-falls.swimming: Not at the falls; the creek is protected
/maryland/thurmont/cunningham-falls.accessibility: Boardwalk Trail is fully accessible and ends at the base of the falls; Lower Trail is passable with a large-wheeled stroller
sources: NPS: Exploring Cunningham Falls State Park

/colorado/nederland/boulder-falls.hike: Closed indefinitely: the City of Boulder closed the Boulder Falls area after a late-2024 rockfall and plans a new viewing platform; do not enter the closed trail
sources: City of Boulder: new visitor access for Boulder Falls (Jan. 2026)

/colorado/granby/adams-falls.hike: About 3/4 mile round trip from the East Inlet Trailhead near Grand Lake on the East Inlet and Adams Falls trails
/colorado/granby/adams-falls.parking: East Inlet Trailhead at the end of West Portal Road, Grand Lake
/colorado/granby/adams-falls.fees: RMNP entrance pass required year-round: $30 per vehicle for 1 day or $35 for 7 days (card only); from May 22 to Oct. 12, 2026 a timed entry reservation ($2 Recreation.gov fee) was also needed to enter between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m.; display the reservation on the dashboard at East Inlet
/colorado/granby/adams-falls.dogs: No pets on Rocky Mountain National Park trails
sources: NPS: Rocky Mountain fees and passes

/colorado/estes-park/ouzel-falls.hike: 5.4-mile round trip (2.7 miles each way) from the Wild Basin Ranger Station, passing Copeland Falls and Calypso Cascades
/colorado/estes-park/ouzel-falls.parking: Wild Basin Trailhead at the Wild Basin Ranger Station (8,500 feet)
/colorado/estes-park/ouzel-falls.fees: RMNP entrance pass required year-round: $30 per vehicle for 1 day or $35 for 7 days (card only); from May 22 to Oct. 12, 2026 a timed entry reservation ($2 Recreation.gov fee) was also needed to enter between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m.
/colorado/estes-park/ouzel-falls.dogs: No pets on Rocky Mountain National Park trails
sources: NPS: Rocky Mountain list of hiking trails
NPS: Rocky Mountain fees and passes

/colorado/estes-park/alberta-falls.hike: 1.6-mile round trip (0.8 mile each way) from Glacier Gorge Junction on Bear Lake Road
/colorado/estes-park/alberta-falls.parking: Glacier Gorge Trailhead fills early; the free Bear Lake shuttle runs from the Park & Ride in summer
/colorado/estes-park/alberta-falls.fees: RMNP entrance pass required year-round: $30 per vehicle for 1 day or $35 for 7 days (card only); from May 22 to Oct. 12, 2026 a timed entry reservation ($2 Recreation.gov fee) was also needed to enter between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. Bear Lake Road needed a Timed Entry + Bear Lake Road reservation from 5 a.m. to 6 p.m., May 22 to Oct. 18, 2026
/colorado/estes-park/alberta-falls.dogs: No pets on Rocky Mountain National Park trails
sources: NPS: Rocky Mountain list of hiking trails
NPS: Rocky Mountain fees and passes

/colorado/estes-park/chasm-falls.hike: About 0.1 mile walk down from a pullout on Old Fall River Road; 2.2 miles round trip from the winter closure gate when the road is closed
/colorado/estes-park/chasm-falls.parking: Pullouts along one-way, gravel Old Fall River Road
/colorado/estes-park/chasm-falls.fees: RMNP entrance pass required year-round: $30 per vehicle for 1 day or $35 for 7 days (card only); from May 22 to Oct. 12, 2026 a timed entry reservation ($2 Recreation.gov fee) was also needed to enter between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m.
/colorado/estes-park/chasm-falls.dogs: No pets on Rocky Mountain National Park trails
sources: NPS: Rocky Mountain fees and passes

/colorado/estes-park/copeland-falls.hike: 0.6-mile round trip along the St. Vrain River from the Wild Basin Trailhead to Upper and Lower Copeland Falls
/colorado/estes-park/copeland-falls.parking: Wild Basin Trailhead at the Wild Basin Ranger Station
/colorado/estes-park/copeland-falls.fees: RMNP entrance pass required year-round: $30 per vehicle for 1 day or $35 for 7 days (card only); from May 22 to Oct. 12, 2026 a timed entry reservation ($2 Recreation.gov fee) was also needed to enter between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m.
/colorado/estes-park/copeland-falls.dogs: No pets on Rocky Mountain National Park trails
/colorado/estes-park/copeland-falls.swimming: No; NPS warns of fast-moving water and slippery rocks
sources: NPS: Rocky Mountain fees and passes

/colorado/estes-park/cascade-falls.hike: 7-mile round trip (3.5 miles each way) on the North Inlet Trail from the North Inlet Trailhead near Grand Lake
/colorado/estes-park/cascade-falls.parking: North Inlet Trailhead near Grand Lake
/colorado/estes-park/cascade-falls.fees: RMNP entrance pass required year-round: $30 per vehicle for 1 day or $35 for 7 days (card only); from May 22 to Oct. 12, 2026 a timed entry reservation ($2 Recreation.gov fee) was also needed to enter between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m.
/colorado/estes-park/cascade-falls.dogs: No pets on Rocky Mountain National Park trails
sources: NPS: Rocky Mountain list of hiking trails
NPS: Rocky Mountain fees and passes

/colorado/evergreen/elk-falls.hike: Elk Falls Trail in Staunton State Park is listed at 12 miles; CPW says the average hiker takes four to five hours for the full trip
/colorado/evergreen/elk-falls.fees: Staunton State Park daily vehicle pass $10 to $15, or $4 per person
/colorado/evergreen/elk-falls.dogs: Leashed dogs allowed; CPW lists the Elk Falls Trail as dog friendly
/colorado/evergreen/elk-falls.accessibility: Staunton runs a Track Chair (all-terrain wheelchair) program on designated trails by reservation
sources: Colorado Parks and Wildlife: Staunton activities and trails

/utah/snyderville/doughnut-falls.hike: Starts at the Donut Falls Trailhead, 8.9 miles up Big Cottonwood Canyon (Highway 190), reached by a short gravel road
/utah/snyderville/doughnut-falls.parking: Small dirt lot with limited spaces and two accessible vault toilets
/utah/snyderville/doughnut-falls.fees: Day use $10 per vehicle for 3 days, $20 for 7 days or $60 per season; interagency passes accepted
/utah/snyderville/doughnut-falls.dogs: No dogs or other domestic animals (protected watershed)
/utah/snyderville/doughnut-falls.swimming: No swimming, wading or playing in the water (protected watershed)

/georgia/blairsville/desoto-falls.hike: Two waterfalls on the DeSoto Falls trails from the day-use lot in the DeSoto Falls Scenic Area off US 19/129
/georgia/blairsville/desoto-falls.parking: Day-use lot immediately on the left after entering the recreation area
/georgia/blairsville/desoto-falls.fees: $5 per vehicle per day, paid on site with the Recreation.gov app; Chattahoochee-Oconee Forest Annual Pass ($25) accepted

/tennessee/benton/benton-falls.hike: Benton Falls Trail is 1.5 miles each way (3 miles round trip) to the 65-foot falls from the Chilhowee Recreation Area
/tennessee/benton/benton-falls.parking: Chilhowee day-use area, 7.2 miles up Forest Road 77 from US 64

/oregon/sisters/koosah-falls.hike: Viewpoint near the Koosah Falls parking area; the Waterfalls Loop Trail (#3503) links Koosah and Sahalie Falls and can be looped with the McKenzie River Trail
/oregon/sisters/koosah-falls.parking: Koosah Falls lot at the Ice Cap Campground turnoff off Highway 126; do not park on the highway shoulder; lots are not plowed in winter
/oregon/sisters/koosah-falls.dogs: On a leash no longer than 6 feet within developed sites
/oregon/sisters/koosah-falls.bestSeason: Snow-free months; winter trail is unmarked and snowshoes are recommended

/south-carolina/walhalla/isaqueena-falls.hike: 0.4-mile round trip on a natural and boardwalk path from the Stumphouse Tunnel parking area to a viewing platform for the 100-foot cascade
/south-carolina/walhalla/isaqueena-falls.parking: Stumphouse Tunnel Park lot, 6.9 miles west of Walhalla on SC 28
/south-carolina/walhalla/isaqueena-falls.fees: $5 per vehicle (cash or QR-code online payment)

/idaho/kimberly/twin-falls.hike: Viewpoint with interpretive panels in Idaho Power's 10-acre Twin Falls Park, two miles upstream of Shoshone Falls
/idaho/kimberly/twin-falls.parking: Park lot off Falls Avenue; open daily 8 a.m. to dark
/idaho/kimberly/twin-falls.fees: Day use is free; the reservable picnic shelter is $75 per day
/idaho/kimberly/twin-falls.accessibility: Idaho Power lists the park as accessible, with restrooms

/virginia/grottoes/doyles-river-falls.hike: 3.3-mile round trip from the Doyles River parking area (Skyline Drive mile 81.1) on the blue-blazed Doyles River Trail to the upper and lower falls, with a stream crossing
/virginia/grottoes/doyles-river-falls.parking: Doyles River parking area at Skyline Drive mile 81.1
/virginia/grottoes/doyles-river-falls.fees: Shenandoah National Park entrance pass required: $30 per private vehicle for 7 days, $15 per person on foot or bike; cashless (card only); annual and interagency passes accepted
/virginia/grottoes/doyles-river-falls.dogs: Allowed on a leash no longer than 6 feet
/virginia/grottoes/doyles-river-falls.accessibility: Trail does not meet ADA accessibility guidelines
